title: AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner (CLF-C02) Study Guide
description: AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner is the foundational AWS certification. Exam CLF-C02 is 65 questions in 90 minutes — 50 scored and 15 unscored trial questions — scored out of 1000 with 700 to pass, and costs $100 USD. It covers cloud concepts, security and compliance, core AWS technology and services, and billing, pricing and support models. It is a breadth exam: you need to recognise what a service does and when it is the right answer, not how to build with it.
audience: Career changers and beginners entering cloud, and non-technical people in sales, finance, procurement or project management who work alongside AWS teams and need to follow the conversation. It also suits IT professionals who want a first AWS credential before the associate exams. AWS suggests up to six months of general exposure to the cloud, but there are no prerequisites and no hands-on requirement.
why_get_it: Cloud Practitioner is the easiest way to get 'AWS certified' on your resume and prove cloud literacy. It's the most accessible AWS cert—no deep technical prerequisites—yet it carries real recognition because AWS is the dominant cloud platform. For beginners it's a confidence-building first win and a foundation for the higher-paying associate exams (Solutions Architect, Developer, SysOps). For non-technical roles, it signals you can speak the language of cloud—services, pricing, and security—which is increasingly expected across sales, finance, and project management in tech.
when_to_get_it: Take Cloud Practitioner if you are new to cloud and want an approachable first AWS certification, or if your role touches AWS without being deeply technical. Two to four weeks of study is typical. If you already have IT experience and a technical goal, many people skip straight to Solutions Architect – Associate (SAA-C03), which carries far more weight with hiring managers — and passing any higher AWS certification renews Cloud Practitioner anyway. The honest case for taking it first is momentum, a clearer map of the service catalogue, and the fact that plenty of non-engineering job postings name it specifically.
exam_format: 65 questions (50 scored, 15 unscored): multiple choice and multiple response. Passing score: 700 (on a scale of 100–1000).
recertification_note: Valid for 3 years. Recertify by passing the current Cloud Practitioner exam, or by earning any higher-level AWS certification, which extends your Cloud Practitioner validity.
salary_note: Cloud Practitioner is an entry credential rather than a salary driver on its own. Cloud support and junior cloud roles for certificate holders commonly fall in the $65K–$90K range, with the national median around $78K. It pays off most as a stepping stone—pairing it with hands-on experience and an associate-level AWS cert (SAA-C03) moves you toward six figures.

study_steps.title: Download the CLF-C02 exam guide
study_steps.description: Get the official AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner (CLF-C02) exam guide. The four domains and their weightings are your roadmap—note that Cloud Technology & Services and Security are two-thirds of the exam.

study_steps.title: Work through a primary video course
study_steps.description: Choose one comprehensive CLF-C02 course and complete it end to end. Stephane Maarek's course on Udemy is the most popular and includes hands-on demos. See the paid resources section.

study_steps.title: Create a free-tier AWS account and explore
study_steps.description: Sign up for the AWS Free Tier and click around the console: launch an EC2 instance, create an S3 bucket, open the Billing dashboard. Hands-on familiarity makes the service questions trivial.

study_steps.title: Use the free AWS digital training
study_steps.description: AWS Skill Builder offers a free Cloud Practitioner Essentials course straight from AWS. Use it to reinforce the official terminology and service descriptions the exam uses.

study_steps.title: Read a study guide for the weak spots
study_steps.description: Keep the Sybex Cloud Practitioner Study Guide handy to go deeper on billing, pricing, and security topics that videos sometimes skim. Use it to close specific gaps.

study_steps.title: Take practice exams
study_steps.description: Work through full-length CLF-C02 practice exams. Aim to score consistently above 85% before booking. Review every miss—many Cloud Practitioner questions hinge on knowing which service does what.

study_steps.title: Schedule and sit the exam
study_steps.description: Register through Pearson VUE or PSI (test center or online proctored). The exam is 90 minutes. It's an approachable exam—most prepared candidates pass on the first attempt.

faq.question: Is AWS Cloud Practitioner worth it?
faq.answer: For beginners and non-technical roles, yes. It's the easiest way to get AWS-certified and prove cloud literacy, and it's a confidence-building first step toward the higher-value associate exams. Technical candidates with experience often skip straight to Solutions Architect Associate.

faq.question: How hard is the CLF-C02 exam?
faq.answer: It's the easiest AWS exam—foundational and broad rather than deep. Most candidates pass with a few weeks of study. Knowing which service does what, plus the basics of pricing and security, gets you most of the way there.

faq.question: Do I need experience before Cloud Practitioner?
faq.answer: No. There are no prerequisites, and it's designed to be accessible to beginners and non-technical professionals. A free-tier AWS account for hands-on clicking is the only 'experience' you really need.

faq.question: How long does it take to study for Cloud Practitioner?
faq.answer: Most candidates spend 2 to 4 weeks part-time. Those with some IT background may be ready in a week or two. A single video course plus practice exams is usually enough.

faq.question: Should I get Cloud Practitioner or go straight to Solutions Architect Associate?
faq.answer: If you have IT experience and a technical goal, many people skip straight to SAA-C03. If you're new to cloud or in a non-technical role, Cloud Practitioner is a low-cost, low-risk way to build a foundation and momentum first.

faq.question: What comes after Cloud Practitioner?
faq.answer: The associate-level AWS certifications: Solutions Architect Associate (most popular), Developer Associate, or SysOps Administrator Associate—depending on whether you lean toward architecture, development, or operations.

faq.question: Does AWS Cloud Practitioner expire?
faq.answer: Yes. It's valid for three years. Recertify by retaking the current exam, or by earning any higher-level AWS certification, which extends your Cloud Practitioner validity automatically.

related_certs.title: AWS Solutions Architect Associate
related_certs.reason: The natural next step. Cloud Practitioner builds the foundation; SAA-C03 is the in-demand, higher-paying associate credential most people target next.

related_certs.title: AWS Developer Associate
related_certs.reason: The associate path for software engineers. A strong follow-on for Cloud Practitioner holders who write code and build cloud-native apps.

related_certs.title: AZ-900: Azure Fundamentals
related_certs.reason: The Microsoft equivalent foundational cloud cert. Many beginners get both to demonstrate cross-cloud literacy.
